messages:
Marta Gómez: Quick sync: canonicalization + compact envelopes follow-up. We need a shadow plan and acceptance KPIs.
Noah Patel: Agreed. Core idea: compute a stable canonical fingerprint at ingress (allowlist attrs -> normalized bytes -> siphash/blake2b -> fingerprint_v1) and carry that in a small header.
Riley Zhang: Benefits: O(1) hot-path work, much lower cardinality downstream joins. Risks: losing ad-hoc filtering for non-indexed attrs. Mitigation: keep sampled traces with full attrs.
Sanjay Rao: Migration: shadow mode for 2 weeks, edge emits fingerprint but doesn't drop fields. Collect metrics: fingerprint_collision_rate, compact_ratio, attribution_loss_rate, reconcile_lag.
Marta Gómez: Operational detail: edge-normalize stage must be deterministic across languages. Publish reference libs and test vectors. Also include version byte in fingerprint header.
Noah Patel: Perf sketch: compute fingerprint by sorting allowed keys, trimming whitespace, lowercasing, concatenating with a separator, and running siphash64 with a seed. Pseudocode in RFC.
Riley Zhang: Backfill: run a 48h replay to seed the small mapping cache so legacy envelopes map to fingerprints for query-time resolution. Keep cache LRU, size bounded.
Sanjay Rao: Acceptance criteria to flip: 1) fingerprint_collision_rate < 0.01% over shadow window, 2) attribution_loss_rate < 0.1%, 3) compact_ratio >= 75% on targeted routes, 4) reconcile_lag_p99 < 10m.
Marta Gómez: Runbook: enable shadow for one region, monitor KPIs for 48h, expand gradually. If attribution_loss_rate spikes, revert for affected routes.
ingest-bot: CI: feature/attr-canonicalization unit tests passed and will schedule shadow run: 2025-06-02T03:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
Noah Patel: I'll draft the RFC with test vectors and perf microbenchmarks. Riley will build load tests.
Riley Zhang: I'll add dashboards for compact_ratio and attr_pending_ratio. Also simulate cache miss storm to validate fallback.
Marta Gómez: Thanks — RFC review scheduled Wed 9am PT. Please add acceptance checklist and rollback steps.
